h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, י״ד Ki Savo, 14
Moshe’s Rebukes Repair Each Soul and Reveal Hidden Consolation

p: regarding the curses of Toras Kohanim;
but in those of Mishneh Torah one may stop.
These are said in the plural,
and Moshe said them from the mouth of the Almighty;
and these are said in the singular,
and Moshe said them from his own mouth."
for it gave earlier the reason
מוּסַר ה׳ בְּנִי אַל תִּמְאָס וְגוֹמֵר (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יא)
'My son, do not despise the discipline of Hashem, etc.'" (Mishlei 3:11).
And with the rebuke of Moshe Rabbeinu,
is it permitted to despise and to loathe?
הֲלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁתּוֹכָחוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים
Surely, just as the rebukes of Toras Kohanim
הָיָה כְּאָב אֶת בֵּן יִרְצֶה (שָׁם ג, יב)
were "as a father the son in whom he delights" (ibid. 3:12)
and "he who loves him disciplines him early" (ibid. 13:24),
so too the rebukes of Moshe Rabbeinu,
he is called a lover of Yisrael.
say even one word on his own?
Surely everything was from Hashem, may He be blessed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג ז, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 7a):
"For there is not found a word in the Torah
from the mouth of Moshe on his own;
and this is what they established:
Moshe said from his own mouth
And it says there a secret
about the level of "his own mouth."
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רסה, א)
And so it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 265a):
that even a single small letter in the Torah
But we have pointed out, and it is well:
'of himself' we did not learn, etc.,"
and as it is written there.
And what kind of reason is this,
that Moshe said them from his own mouth,
so that it should be permitted to stop in them?
because they were said in the singular;
only, why were they said in the singular?
"because Moshe said them from his own mouth."
And it is that Hashem, may He be blessed,
so that they be aroused to rectify the blemish,
so that there not come upon them
And before Hashem, may He be blessed,
they are all surveyed in a single glance
which Hashem, may He be blessed, said,
for to all of them was said
and therefore one may not stop in them,
'My son, do not despise the discipline of Hashem,
and do not loathe His rebuke'";
and in Rashi, in the name of Maseches Sofrim:
do not make the rebuke into pieces."
with the curses of Mishneh Torah;
for Mishneh Torah is the seventh book
of the seven books of the Torah,
"'She has hewn out her seven pillars' (Mishlei 9:1)
these are the seven books of the Torah";
and in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 38a) it is expounded:
"'She has hewn out her seven pillars'
these are the seven days of Creation,"
which correspond to the seven lower attributes,
כִּמְבוֹאָר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פט, ב)
as explained in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 89b);
for it is written, "For six days
and it is not written "in six,"
corresponds to the attribute of Malchus;
we call it the Oral Torah."
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רסא, א)
And so it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 261a):
'Moshe said them from his own mouth,' etc.
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,
וְהוּא אִיקְּרֵי תּוֹרָה וּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
and it is called Torah and Mishneh Torah, etc."
is the aspect of the Oral Torah
and for this reason there were written in this book
and there was included in them
that came to rectify the "abundance of anger" (Koheles 1:18)
And this is the meaning of
"Moshe said them from his own mouth":
that Hashem, may He be blessed, commanded him
on the level of "his own mouth."
And this is what Tosafos says:
And therefore he said them in the singular:
that is, that there are rectifications in this
for each individual on his own,
and they have no connection to one another;
and therefore it is permitted to stop in them,
and is not connected to its neighbor.
And just as there came in this parshah
and they correspond to eleven tribes,
and although they were all said to all Yisrael,
a different matter specifically to clarify,
and there is a break between the passages
so too the rebukes were also said
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק בְּיִחוּד
for each one has a specific matter
And therefore the blessings too were said
Hashem, may He be blessed, gave the assistance
so that he should have no hindrance
from the affairs of this world
to walk in the ways of Hashem.
And for this reason it is permitted to stop
in the curses of Mishneh Torah,
and there is no issue here of "do not loathe,"

p: who gave the reason that one does not stop
"because one does not say a blessing
why in the curses of Mishneh Torah one may stop,
and what kind of reason is it,
"and these are said in the singular,
But we have already raised the question
"because one does not say a blessing, etc.,"
and in Tosafos it is brought from Maseches Sofrim:
"A person must bless over the bad
just as he blesses over the good";
and it derives this from many verses.
So why does it say here
that one does not say a blessing
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז, ב)
based on what they said in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 17b):
it is written, 'Hashem is righteous in all His ways,'
וּכְתִיב וְחָסִיד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו (תְּהִלִּים קמה, יז)
and it is written, 'and kind in all His deeds' (Tehillim 145:17).
הֵם דְּרָכָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
is the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and in all His ways He is righteous,
the Holy One, blessed be He, does not act
beyond the letter of the law;
judgment, of which 'truth' is not written
the Holy One, blessed be He, acts
beyond the letter of the law."
But when it comes to the realm of deed,
then Hashem, may He be blessed, acts
beyond the letter of the law;
and this is the meaning of
And therefore over the deeds of Hashem, may He be blessed,
one must bless over the bad
just as he blesses over the good,
is beyond the letter of the law,
and one must accept them with joy.
This is not so with the passages of rebuke,
שֶׁהֵם דְּרָכָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
which are the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and in them He does not act
beyond the letter of the law;
only when it comes to deed
will Hashem, may He be blessed, act
beyond the letter of the law,
and it will not be so.
and this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
"because one does not say a blessing
in truth it will not be so,
for Hashem, may He be blessed, will act
beyond the letter of the law;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קיד, ב)
and as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 114b):
the rod is always in His hand
like a father who raises the rod
so that he improve his way.
And over this one does not say a blessing
He acts beyond the letter of the law,
And this applies to the curses of Toras Kohanim;
but regarding the curses of Mishneh Torah,
it is brought in the Zohar Chadash (on this parshah):
"All the promises and consolations of Yisrael
a king who loves his son, etc.;
so the Holy One, blessed be He
but they are many good things;
which were all in severe judgment, etc."
And it is as we see,
the Name Havayah is written with every curse;
"The Holy One, blessed be He, never
associates His Name with evil, etc.:
אֶלָּא וְלַחוֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ה)
וַהֲרֵי דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְכִּיר
So the Holy One, blessed be He, does not mention
which is the Name of the attribute of judgment,
all the more so the Name Havayah,
which is the Name of mercy;
the Name Havayah in every verse.
they are in truth good things and consolations;
and the Zohar Chadash explains (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo)
as being good things and consolations,
and at the end it concludes:
as it is written, 'so that you may succeed, etc.' (Devarim 29:8);
And this is as the holy Zohar explains
whoever is on the path of understanding.
Moshe said from his own mouth":
that is, they are akin to
and they are not calamities at all,
for they are all good things and consolations;
that is, when Hashem, may He be blessed, acts,
you should know that all is in mercy,
for Hashem, may He be blessed, acts
beyond the letter of the law.
And for this reason there does not apply here
the reason that one does not say a blessing
since this is not calamity at all.
And according to what was said,
it is possible that the reason it gave,
is an answer according to the view
מִדִּכְתִיב מוּסַר ה׳ בְּנִי אַל תִּמְאָס
because it is written, "My son, do not despise the discipline of Hashem,
and do not loathe His rebuke"
do not make it into pieces;
and since they were said in the singular,
it is permitted to stop in them,
"because one does not say a blessing
to this it gave the answer,
"and these Moshe said from his own mouth"
and they come to rectify the "abundance of anger,"
and they are all good things and consolations,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
as written in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo);
and it is permitted to say a blessing over them,
and therefore it is permitted to stop in them.
And likewise it mentioned in this parshah
and the blessings were not written in the Torah,
But the blessings were said then for their time
and were not needed for the generations;
only the "cursed"s were written for the generations,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
as written in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo):
so that the generations be aroused
the blemish that pertains to him.
And when the "abundance of anger" is rectified,
all will be good things and consolations,

p: "And there you shall offer yourselves for sale to your enemies, etc.,
and there will be no buyer" (Devarim 28:68),
And this is based on what is said
בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
in the Zohar Chadash on this parshah (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo):
"'And you shall be sold' is not written,
but 'you shall offer yourselves for sale'
in your heart you will think
for 'there will be no buyer' is written,
and there is no one who can
and all this is at the end of days,
and everything depends on teshuvah, etc."
For this refers to the end,
and then there will be the rectification for the whole community;
and with this comes the rectification
even for the curses of Toras Kohanim,
which are said in the plural,
שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן יִהְיֶה רַק בְּדִמְיוֹן
that they too will be only in imagination:
that they will think that they have gathered against them
there is no one who can rule over you.
And the curses of Toras Kohanim
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
as written in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo);
and then it was not yet the time
for everything to be rectified, each soul in particular,
for it was not the time of the End;
and therefore they were said in the plural,
to rectify in a general way.
with the curses of Mishneh Torah,
which correspond to the Second Temple,
which is such a long time;
and this is so that there be rectified
וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד)
"and none be banished from Him" (Shmuel II 14:14).
And for this they were said in the singular,
for then each soul in particular
will rectify what pertains to his soul
the rectification specific to its tribe.
And this is why it seals at the end
that is, that in the end
the rectification will be done for the community
